annotations.text:
Current layout, recreated from the real CharacterPage.js/.scss.

What it's missing: character name, class, and player name appear nowhere on the page (only in the browser tab title). The purple bar is empty by default.

The ability-score and HP/AC boxes are fixed-width (400px + 500px) and don't fill the row — at real desktop widths this leaves a large dead black gap to the right, which is the empty space you see in your screenshot.

v2 — Roleplay / Combat / Combat Map redesigned (per your scope); Inventory intentionally left as a stub for a later pass.

Working prototype: click the Roleplay / Combat / Inventory / Combat Map pills to switch modes, and click the Action Point stars in Combat mode to test the resource tracker. The masthead color is a tweak (chip above the artboard) standing in for the existing per-character color picker.

"Character Name" / "Class Name" are placeholders — everything else in Roleplay mode (skills, stats, background, notes) is your real data from the screenshot. Combat actions and map zones are illustrative sample content.

Mobile v2 — all four modes, including Inventory this time.

What's different from the desktop version, and why:

• The mode switcher moves to a fixed bottom tab bar (thumb reach) instead of top pills.

• Skills & Flaws can't stay a persistent 300px sidebar at this width — it's now a summary row that opens a slide-up drawer over the screen. Tap "Skills & Flaws" to open it, tap the scrim or the X to close.

• Inventory is redesigned from scratch here: the desktop app's multi-column drag-and-drop board (4 relic slots + 8 backpack slots + a pocket, all side-by-side) doesn't fit a 390px screen, so it's restructured as stacked sections — a 2x2 Relics grid, a scrollable Backpack list, and the Pocket as its own highlighted card. Empty slots are shown honestly rather than hidden.

Working prototype: tap the bottom tabs, the AP stars in Combat, and the Skills & Flaws row.

NEW — Statuses, added to the Vitals card on both Desktop and Mobile.

Working prototype: click a status chip to expand its description and reveal a Remove button; click "Add Status" / "Add" to open the dialog, pick a preset, adjust stacks with +/−, pick a polarity, then confirm.

Scope for this pass (per your answers): character-page display + manual add/remove only. No automated turn-based action-point adjustment yet (haste/slowed granting or removing an action is a rules effect, not wired up here), and no Director's/enemy-page UI yet — that's a separate future redesign. Built generically enough that the same pattern could extend to NPCs/enemies later.

Open decision, intentionally left to you + the coding agent: whether the status catalog is a fixed preset list, fully freeform/custom, or a hybrid (presets + custom fallback, which is what this mockup gestures at with the "Custom…" chip and the note under it). The dialog here only wires up preset selection since two-way text input isn't proven in this canvas tool — the handoff doc flags that a real Add form needs a free-text name/description field for custom statuses.

UPDATED — Vitals card is now a 2x2 stat grid + portrait (Desktop only; the mobile card was already stacked narrow, so it didn't need this).

Layout: top-left HP, top-right AC + XP/Hardness, bottom-left Statuses, bottom-right ability scores (Str/Dex/Int/Cha) — a hairline cross divides the four tiles. To the right of the whole grid, a framed portrait panel spans the full card height.

Why this shape: the first draft stacked everything in one tall column (HP, then AC/XP, then abilities, then Statuses), which read as a 1x4 stack rather than a balanced tile layout and didn't pair related things (HP next to AC/XP; Statuses next to abilities) the way this version does.

The portrait panel is a themed placeholder (no portrait_url field exists in the schema yet, same caveat as the small masthead avatar) with its own edit badge, matching the masthead's pencil-button pattern. Once a real portrait field exists, this is where the character's full art would render; the masthead avatar can stay a small cropped/thumbnail version of the same image.
